svg.text: AI-First Product Operating System — Conceptual Architecture
One cloud system on Azure AI Foundry · three harnesses · one Intelligence Layer · multi-tenant: every layer is scoped to one organisation + product
Harness Surface — the single entry point for people (not for load)
one UI service · many entry types: new product · feature · small change (sentence + screenshot) · bug · incident · tech debt · Design System / theme · spike
intent · outcome · AC · evals · in / OUT scope
grill intent → thin conceptual architecture → Big Plan (backlog)
value slices · MVP-0 route · ticket fields incl. blockers + write-set
SMALL LOOP (one agent group per ticket, in parallel)
clarify → small plan → build → deterministic checks → semantic check → PR
DRIFT CHECKPOINT every N merges: insert tickets, merged work frozen
LIGHT ROUTE: small changes skip step zero
classify entry · context visibility · model tier
tool pick · clarification? · failure class · verdict
rules apply thresholds; answers never branch alone
stateless: grant + context package + pinned skill in,
emit + close out · state lives only in the ledger
scales out: one agent group per claimed ticket
grill · plan · clarify · build · semantic check ·
Model Gateway → Azure AI Foundry only
route by tier + sensitivity · priced per context rebuild
refuses rather than downgrades · spend quota
model version served recorded on every run
Intelligence Layer — the cookbook the agents cook from
per folder · DS rules for UI

seams: open (scoped context package) · emit (candidate, never a verdict) · close (run answers) · admit (rule-based promotion) — every row carries tenant_id + product_id under strict row-level security
TENANT ISOLATION — org → product scoping is resolved from identity at 1.2 and enforced in the ledger, the context package, the grant, the branch and the release gate
rules, schemas and typed decisions first;
agents only where judgement is needed;
the builder is the one place kept free
Delivery trusts only a signed, testable
the Big Plan is a backlog; only the
drift inserts tickets into what remains;
low merges itself; medium and high wait
for a named person with an SLA
cheap models only pay off on a small,
typed reads vs writes make parallel
humans answer, sign, review and release —

Reading order: people enter through one Harness Surface; intake routes each item to the harness it needs; harnesses call the control plane; every model call is a dispatch run by a stateless Stage runner;
context comes only from the Intelligence Layer through open; results go back only through emit and close. The workflow diagram shows the same system as a sequence of steps.

The decision-layer pattern is borrowed from the Jev design notes (TypeSafe). It is built here as rules plus a small Foundry-hosted model, not bought, because every model call must stay inside Foundry.
